subject: Pricing for cross-product expansion — per-token banding & top-up
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightcommerce.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Inquiry: pricing for adding Payments & LiveSearch workloads

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the recent demo — it was helpful. We're evaluating Redwood to power two additional product lines this quarter: Payments fraud scoring (latency-sensitive generation) and LiveSearch embeddings (high-volume). The expected change in our token mix based on the attached projection is ~60% embeddings, ~30% short generations (<50 tokens), and ~10% longer form generations.

Can you share a proposal that includes:
- per-token rate bands for monthly commit tiers (0-5B, 5-20B, 20B+)
- a top-up/top-off approach if we overshoot commit mid-quarter (we want predictable unit economics)
- any burst-capacity or transient capacity pricing for big Black-Friday–like windows
- whether embeddings are blended or should be priced separately (we may want a separate embeddings bucket)

Procurement needs a clear commit vs pay-as-you-go comparison and how additional workloads would be treated if we add more teams later this year. Ideally we get a target proposal by end of next week. Attaching the RFP and a sample traffic projection.

Best,
Sarah Lee
Director, Platform
BrightCommerce

Attachments: BrightCommerce_RFP_Q4.pdf (pdf), traffic_sample.csv (csv)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: pricing for adding Payments & LiveSearch workloads

Hi Sarah — great to see the projection, thanks for sending.

High-level response and next steps below — I attached a short note with an illustrative banding to get the conversation started (initial-pricing-note.pdf). Quick ask: could you confirm the expected committed term (12 vs 24 months) and whether the two workloads should live under one commit or separate commits per product? That will materially change the blended rates.

Prelim banding (illustrative):
- 0–5B tokens / month: baseline PAYG-equivalent rate
- 5–20B tokens / month: ~15–25% discount vs baseline
- 20B+ tokens / month: additional 10–15% (deeper band)

Embeddings: recommend a separate per-embedding unit tier if embeddings will be >40% of volume — we can offer a more aggressive SKU there.

Top-up approach: we typically allow an in-quarter top-up at a premium (example +8–12%) and apply the committed tiers retroactively at quarter close for billing reconciliation. For burst windows we can provision burst credits tied to a short-term capacity reservation (one-time fee) or add burst pricing as a premium on top of normal rates.

If you can confirm term and whether you want separate SKUs for embeddings, I will route a refined proposal to Karthik and Finance for a formal commit structure and an optional DocuSign for signature.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Attachment: initial-pricing-note.pdf
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Inquiry: pricing for adding Payments & LiveSearch workloads — need guidance on expansion pricing

Team — forwarding BrightCommerce's ask (below). Key points: two new workloads, heavy embeddings share, want commit vs PAYG comparison + top-up policy. Sarah wants a target proposal by EOW.

Questions for pricing/leadership (short):
1) Recommend single blended commit (all teams under one agreement) or separate commits per product for more aggressive embeddings pricing?
2) For in-quarter top-ups: we typically do +10% premium; ok to keep that band? Any appetite to lower to 8% for enterprise deals?
3) Burst capacity: can we offer a one-time reserved burst credit (e.g., 100m tokens) vs time-bound provisioning? If so, what pricing is reasonable to offer here?

I'm proposing Karthik draft 2 commit options (blended vs separate embeddings SKU) and Marissa loop procurement language. Aditya — will need an exception if we pull below standard pricing bands.

Thanks,
Monica

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@brightcommerce.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Inquiry: pricing for adding Payments & LiveSearch workloads
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Inquiry: pricing for adding Payments & LiveSearch workloads — proposed commit structures

Monica / Marissa — draft proposal below (numbers are illustrative; final to be approved by Finance/RevOps). I've attached a spreadsheet with the two recommended structures (commit_structures.xlsx).

Option A — Blended commit (single agreement, blended by estimated mix)
- Term: 12 months
- Commit tiers (monthly tokens):
  * 0–5B: $0.000025 per token (baseline)
  * 5–20B: $0.000018 per token (~28% discount)
  * 20B+: $0.000014 per token (~44% discount)
- Embeddings: charged as separate SKU at $0.000040 per embedding unit for 0–5B; 5–20B: $0.000032; 20B+: $0.000025
- In-quarter top-up: allowed at +10% on the relevant per-token rate; reconciliation at quarter close to the effective committed tier
- Burst credits: one-time purchase available (e.g., 100M tokens) at a 20% premium to baseline; or time-bound provisioning via Dedicated burst for SLA-backed capacity (priced separately)

Option B — Separate embeddings commit (two SKUs)
- Separate commit for embeddings with more aggressive pricing if client commits >40% of volume to embeddings
- Provides clearer unit economics for BrightCommerce's LiveSearch product

Revenue ops note: if client requests lower top-up premium (8%) or deeper bands for long term (24 months), we need RevOps sign-off. For enterprise deals we can consider a modest concession on top-up in exchange for an upfront non-refundable burst credit purchase.

If these look good, Monica should present both options to the customer and indicate that we can convert the selected option into a DocuSign-ready Addendum.

Thanks — Karthik

Attachment: commit_structures.xlsx

Subject: Re: Inquiry: pricing for adding Payments & LiveSearch workloads — Redwood proposal

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the details and the projection. Based on internal review we've put together two clean options for BrightCommerce (summary below). I've also attached a concise pricing sheet (proposed-pricing-sheet.xlsx) and a DocuSign link for the Addendum if you'd like to proceed.

Summary (TL;DR)
Option A — Blended commit (recommended if you want single agreement):
- 12‑month term; blended tiers by monthly token volume; sample per-token rates: 0–5B $0.000025; 5–20B $0.000018; 20B+ $0.000014
- Embeddings priced as a separate SKU but billed under the same agreement; deeper bands if embeddings >40%
- In-quarter top-up: +10% premium; quarter-end reconciliation to committed tiers
- Burst credits available as one-time purchase (example 100M tokens) at a premium or Dedicated burst for SLA-backed capacity (price on request)

Option B — Separate embeddings commit (recommended if you need predictable per-embedding costs):
- Separate embeddings SKU and commit with more aggressive per-unit pricing at higher commitments

Next steps:
1) Tell me which option you prefer and confirm term (12 vs 24 months).
2) If you want us to lower the in-quarter top-up premium (8% vs 10%), we can discuss a trade-off (e.g., non-refundable burst credit or slightly higher commit).
3) I can route a DocuSign addendum once you confirm; link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123

If you'd like, we can set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the numbers and the contract language so Procurement has clear language on top-ups and burst credits.

Best,
Monica Patel
